item.title: How Micah Ford flipped ignominious era for Stanford football into his personal legacy
item.description: Micah Ford #20 of the Stanford Cardinal looks on before a game against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets on Sept. 26, 2026 at Stanford Stadium in Palo Alto, Calif. (Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Micah Ford has witnessed the lows of this Stanford football era. In November 2024, as a freshman, he watched from the California Memorial Stadium sideline as quarterback Fernando Mendoza went "98 yards with my boys" to lead an epic Big Game comeback, handing Stanford its first four-game losing streak against Cal since 2005. He was in the building four months later, when recently hired general manager Andrew Luck fired Troy Taylor, the head coach who had recruited him, citing the need for a "reset" after an investigation concluded that Taylor had bullied and belittled female staffers. Ford saw all of it. The 3-9 season in 2024. The 4-8 campaign a year ago. The slow start this season. He played for one head coach as a freshman (Taylor), then another as a sophomore (interim Frank Reich), and now another as a junior playing for first-year head coach Tavita Pritchard. Chaos and turmoil were all he knew. Midway through October, the feeling couldn't have been much better. The Cardinal were 2-4, and each blowout loss looked worse than the last. His team lost those games by a combined 172 points. Ford, the engine of the offense at running back, wasn't producing. But after that 58-7 loss to then-No. 6 Notre Dame on Oct. 10, something changed. Stanford, led by Ford's sudden emergence, became an unrecognizable football team. The first six games of Ford's season: 95 carries, 350 yards (3.7 yards per carry) and four rushing touchdowns. The last five: 108 carries, 701 yards (6.5 YPC) and nine rushing touchdowns. His yardage totals, including receptions, in each of those games were 231, 208, 120, 150 and 156. He's been the most consistent presence for an offense that desperately needed it under fourth-year running backs coach Malcolm Agnew. Ford's success directly led to Stanford's (6-5, 4-4 ACC) success. The Cardinal have won four of their last five games. They destroyed Cal 44-28 in Saturday's Big Game and earned bowl-game eligibility for the first time since 2018. Looking back, Ford can easily say it was all worth it. "To be at a program where, obviously, I didn't have success early, and then to see it gel into the program that we knew it could be," Ford said Saturday, "it's kind of just, like, I'm at a loss of words for it. "Honestly, there was no way we were leaving without that axe today," he added, after rushing for 151 yards and two touchdowns. "I don't know how long (it's been since) Stanford kept it two years in a row. It's probably been a little while." Ford is correct. The last time Stanford won consecutive games against Cal was in 2018, the last of a dominant nine-year Big Game run. Following that season, the Bears won five of six matchups from 2019-2024. item.title: Bills-Chiefs showdown tops NFL Thanksgiving holiday slate
item.description: Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes, left, and Buffalo quarterback Josh Allen, right, will lead their clubs into an NFL Thanksgiving holiday showdown with the best record in the NFL's American Conference up for grabs (David Eulitt) Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes and Buffalo superstar Josh Allen face a Thursday showdown on the US Thanksgiving holiday that will have a major impact on the NFL playoff picture. The Bills own the AFC's best record at 9-1 and beating the Chiefs (8-2) would help ensure a home-field edge in the post-season. "We know what type of team they are," Allen said. "They've been one of the best teams in the league the last 10 years. So, you've got to play your best." Mahomes, whose club shares the AFC West division lead with Denver, hopes to snap Buffalo's six-game win streak. "It will be a great challenge for us. We're excited for it," Mahomes said. "You know it's going to take your best football. "Every time we play each other, it always comes down to the end of the game. It's about who makes the big plays in the big moments. It's always exciting. It's always fun." The Bills have averaged 31 points in their win streak while the Chiefs have won three in a row with 34 or more points each game. Allen's Bills and Mahomes's Chiefs are 5-5 in all-time meetings, but it's not so even when it comes to realizing and crushing title hopes. Allen and the Bills are 5-1 in regular-season matchups against Kansas City but Mahomes and the Chiefs are 4-0 in playoff games against Buffalo. The Chiefs have won three Super Bowls and lost two others in the past seven seasons while the Bills have not reached the Super Bowl since losing four in a row from 1991-1994 and were eliminated from the playoffs by Kansas City in four of the past six seasons. "It's the most important one because it's the next one," Allen said of the game. "All the seeding implications, that is what it is. We're just trying to find a way to go 1-0 each week." Cold, windy and rainy conditions are forecast for the contest. "I take pride in being able to throw the ball in any conditions," Mahomes said. The Bills-Chiefs contest tops five games to be played around the US Thanksgiving holiday. Green Bay will visit the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday in a matchup of 6-4 clubs while Thursday also sees Philadelphia at Dallas and a showdown for the NFC North lead when Chicago visits Detroit. Both are 8-2 with the Bears having won five games in a row and Detroit's streak at six. item.title: Paul Pierce Admits 2013 Trade Built Current Celtics Core
item.description: Neville E. Guard-Imagn Images The Boston Celtics won the 2024 NBA title, but the foundation was laid when the franchise traded away its biggest star. Paul Pierce, the man who led the team to victory in 2008, says he has zero regrets about leaving in 2013. He knows the picks Boston received from that deal turned into the two players who finally brought the trophy back. The Trade That Changed Everything Back in 2013, the Brooklyn Nets were desperate and desperate teams make mistakes. They traded for Pierce and Kevin Garnett, giving up three unprotected first-round picks and a pick swap. The Nets project failed hard, and the assets Boston got in return became the keys to the kingdom. According to HITC , Pierce told the Amongst Legends podcast that the trade was handled with total transparency. He respected the process even though it meant leaving Boston. When the Nets finished with a 21-61 record in 2016, Boston used the number three overall pick to draft Jaylen Brown. The next year, the Celtics exercised their pick swap after Brooklyn had the worst record in the league. In the 2017 Draft, Danny Ainge traded down to let the Sixers select Markelle Fultz while the Lakers chose Lonzo Ball. Boston then swooped in to select Jayson Tatum with the third pick. Those two young stars led the team to a championship in 2024, defeating the Mavericks in the Finals. Pierce Owns The Legacy Many fans might think trading Pierce was a mistake, but he sees it differently now. He says the current success of the franchise rests on the foundation his departure created. A Look Back at California Roots Conner Henry, a native of Claremont, California, is part of that long history. He was selected by the Houston Rockets in the 1988 NBA Draft, but he had signed with Boston in 1987. His time with the team was short, lasting only until he was cut that fall. During his stay, Henry averaged 2.7 points per game. AOL.com notes that the Celtics have sought talent from nearly every U.S. state since their early days.

item.title: Cleveland Guardians Add Lefty Starter on $17.5 Million Deal
item.description: Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Kris Bubic (40) throws a pitch against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images The Cleveland Guardians made their first significant free-agent addition of the winter on Tuesday, agreeing to terms with left-hander Kris Bubic on a one-year, $17.5 million contract, according to multiple reports. The deal, which is pending a physical, is the largest one-year guarantee in franchise history and gives Cleveland a familiar AL Central arm to bolster a rotation that already features Parker Messick and Gavin Williams. Bubic, 29, was a 2025 American League All-Star with the Royals, posting a career-best 2.55 ERA over 116⅓ innings that season. His 2026 campaign was far more limited. Elbow and shoulder issues sidelined him for much of the year; he finished with a 3.76 ERA across 55 innings split between Kansas City and the Dodgers after a deadline trade. When healthy, he has shown a five-pitch mix built around a rising four-seam fastball, a firm changeup, and a pair of breaking balls, along with a delivery that has historically generated soft contact and ground balls. For Cleveland, the signing fits a clear priority. The Guardians entered the offseason looking to add starting pitching depth after a season in which they were the only team in baseball to have four pitchers make at least 30 starts. Bubic is expected to slot into the middle of a group that also includes Messick (2026 AL Rookie of the Year and Cy Young finalist), Williams (AL strikeout leader), Tanner Bibee, and several depth options. Outside the Bubic agreement, Cleveland’s offseason activity has been quiet and roster-focused. At the non-tender deadline, they non-tendered utility man David Fry, agreed to deals with relievers Matt Festa and Colin Holderman plus outfielder Blake Perkins to avoid arbitration, and have signed minor-league free agents (including right-hander Jairo Iriarte and left-hander Antoine Kelly). They also added several players to the 40-man roster and claimed José Tena off waivers. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire December 1, the remaining window for additional moves is short . Bubic gives the Guardians an upside left-handed starter on a prove-it deal while they evaluate further pitching or lineup needs.

item.title: NFL Clears DK Metcalf Of Suspension After Sunday Ejection
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The National Football League has decided against suspending Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf after he was ejected during Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. This ruling comes despite Metcalf committing two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties that led to his removal from the game late in the third quarter. The league determined that a suspension was not warranted for the incident where Metcalf allegedly tried to poke Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. While the suspension is off the table, the league will still review the conduct to see if a fine is necessary. Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy addressed the situation during his Monday media availability, noting that he and Metcalf had spoken about the event. McCarthy described the conversations between the two as “productive” and stated that any further discipline from the team would be kept internal. “Life’s about learning situations,” McCarthy said. He also expressed his belief in second chances, noting that he would judge Metcalf based on their personal interactions rather than just the penalty flags. A History of Discipline This ejection marks the third time in his eight-season career that Metcalf has been thrown out of a game. The final two games of the 2025 regular season carry a suspension for the player due to behavior stemming from a physical altercation with a Lions fan in Detroit. The financial toll on the player has been significant, with his fines totaling a whopping $245,647 according to reports. This total excludes an extra $555,555 fine associated with the two-game suspension resulting from the Lions fan altercation. After Sunday’s game, Metcalf exited the locker room without talking to reporters, though he came back to speak with the media on Monday. ProFootballTalk states that he rejected claims he intended to poke Cooper DeJean in the eye. With just one catch on four targets for two yards before ejection, the 28-year-old receiver struggled to find his rhythm this season. In 10 games, the two-time Pro Bowler has secured 36 of his 74 targets, accumulating 434 yards and only two touchdowns. Looking Ahead to Denver Metcalf remains on the Steelers’ active roster as they prepare for their next matchup. The team has a short week to recover before hosting the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. The game is scheduled for Friday, Nov. 27, with kickoff set for 3 p.m. ET. RotoBaller indicates that Metcalf currently sits as the WR40 in half-PPR scoring.

item.title: Dyson Daniels Proves The League Wrong On Value
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Dyson Daniels is the Atlanta Hawks’ most valuable player, not Jalen Johnson, because he drives wins without shooting. Soaring Down South reported that Daniels holds a staggering +18.0 on/off net rating to start the year. This number is the best on the team. The league thinks a shooter is needed to win. Daniels is changing that view with his defense and speed. He impacts winning in every way except shooting, which is a rare skill set. The Thompson twins are the only other players who succeed this way, but both are struggling this season. Amen Thompson has a -9.7 on/off rating with the Rockets, while Ausar sits at +2.2 with the Pistons. Daniels has surpassed both of them. A Deal That Saves The Hawks Money Daniels remains on a team-friendly deal of $25 million per year through the 2029-2030 season. He will have the 35th-highest salary in the league that year, making it the 23rd-lowest contract. Other players in his $20-30 million range include Damian Lillard, Herb Jones, and PJ Washington. Daniels is only 23 years old, one year younger than Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg. By the time his contract ends after the 2030 season, he will be 27 and entering his prime. The contract gives the Hawks an advantage over other teams.

item.title: Mahomes And Reid Show Chiefs Pride Supports Kansas City Current
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Kansas City Chiefs did not wait for a press release to show support for their city. Patrick Mahomes and Andy Reid made their stance clear on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium. While the team prepared for a matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, the focus shifted to a family moment that celebrated a local soccer title. Mahomes, dressed in his full uniform, stopped to greet his wife and children. This act of love happened right before kickoff on a cold November afternoon. A Family Moment on the Sideline The video of the reunion spread fast across social media after the league shared it. Mahomes was already in his red No. 15 jersey when he walked over to the sideline. His children were bundled up in warm coats against the chill. One daughter wore a pale pink puffer coat while the other stood close. The quarterback bent down to wrap his arms around both kids for hugs and kisses. He then turned his attention to Brittany Mahomes, who wore a long black coat. She reached up to touch his face before they shared a kiss. The NFL posted the clip on X with a simple note about the moment. They wrote, “@PatrickMahomes getting some pregame love from his favorite people,” according to Sports Illustrated . Fans React to the Tribute Local fans saw the connection between the NFL champion and the NWSL champions immediately. Brittany Mahomes had already shared photos of the Kansas City Current winning their title. Her husband and the head coach supported her, and the community took notice. People watching the feed reacted with warm words about the scene. One person commented, “Okay that hug actually got me,” per Sports Illustrated. Another viewer simply said, “They are adorable.” A third fan summed up the feeling of the day by writing, “pregame with the family hits different.” These comments show how much the city cares about all its teams, not just one. The Chiefs have built a culture that values family and local pride in equal measure. Mahomes and Reid proved that point without saying a word during the game. The team won their match against Arizona with a final score of 34 to 7 on Sunday. Now the squad looks ahead to their next challenge on the road. The Kansas City Chiefs will play the Buffalo Bills on Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 p.m.

item.title: Lakers Target P.J. Washington To Strengthen Frontcourt
item.description: David Richard-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers are making moves to fix their frontcourt before the trade deadline arrives. General manager Rob Pelinka wants to shore up the team’s depth and add a reliable wing player. Reports indicate the club is targeting Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington to fill a specific hole in their rotation. Heavy.com outlines a specific plan where Dallas sends Washington to Los Angeles in exchange for Jarred Vanderbilt, Jaden Hardy, and two future second-round picks. The Mavericks would receive the picks to add assets to their roster while clearing space for other players. This move would reunite Washington with Luka Doncic, his former teammate from Dallas. The Lakers see Washington as the missing piece to help their star trio dominate the playoffs. Why The Lakers Need Washington Los Angeles has struggled to find a consistent two-way player at the forward spot this season. The team needs someone who can guard top scorers and hit open shots without needing the ball. Heavy.com notes that Washington fits this exact profile. Washington is putting up solid numbers this year. While shooting 36.2% from three-point range, he averages 14.0 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. Those stats show he can contribute immediately without disrupting the flow of the offense. The Lakers have been linked to him for a long time, but the salary cap makes it difficult. His $88 million contract is a big hurdle, yet the front office seems willing to take the risk. Backup Center Search Continues While chasing Washington, the Lakers are also looking for a backup center to play behind Walker Kessler. Marc Stein reported Sunday that the team is actively seeking help in the middle. “Lakers have been actively searching for another center to play behind Walker Kessler and general manager Rob Pelinka has all but promised that a move is forthcoming to address that need,” Stein wrote. The team has limited draft capital to use as leverage in these talks. One potential target is Mavericks center Moussa Cissé. Rookie guard Walter Clayton Jr. could be added to Dallas’s roster, which might require moving Cissé, and Stein noted that the Lakers have only three tradeable second‑round picks, highlighting their limited draft capital, though Los Angeles could trade Kevon Looney and a pick for Cissé despite the 24‑year‑old logging just 36 minutes this season. He is a gamble on upside rather than a sure thing. The Trade Deadline Approach Rob Pelinka has made it clear that the team plans to be active before the deadline. He spoke on Spectrum SportsNet about the need to fix issues the team has spotted. “We’ll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see,” Pelinka said during a Spectrum SportsNet interview. The front office knows the roster has gaps that need filling if they want to challenge for a championship.

item.title: Jiri Lehecka leads Czechs to Davis Cup quarter-final victory over 2022 winners Canada
item.description: Czech No 1 Jiri Lehecka beat Felix Auger-Aliassime 7-6(4) 6-2 to seal a 2-0 quarter-final victory for Czechia over Canada in the Davis Cup . The world No 14’s victory ensured Czechia booked their place in the last four of tennis’ ‘World Cup’ for the first time in more than a decade. Earlier on Tuesday Tomas Mahac beat Liam Draxl 6-2 3-6 6-2 to put the Czechs in front, with Lehecka’s straightforward win meaning there was no need for the dead-rubber doubles match to be played, with Davis Cup ties best of three. Czechia will now play either three-time defending champions Italy, led by Flavio Cobolli, or South Korea, who face off on Wednesday. The semi-final will take place on Friday. Auger-Aliassime, a former world No 4 now ranked 17th, squandered ​nine ⁠break points, including a set ‌point at 5-4 in the opening set, before Lehecka forced a tiebreak. He continued to keep the Canadian under pressure with his aggressive play and powerful forehand, earning an early break before going 3-0 up in the second set, and converted his second match point before celebrating with his teammates. Lehecka said: “It was a super tough match. I was forced to play very well facing some break points and some tough situations. “Felix is such a dangerous player in these conditions, so I’m very proud with the way I converted the chances I had in the first set and also how I was able to improve my game in the second. I think it’s a great win, not just for me but for the whole team and I’m very, very proud of the team.” Earlier Machac, the mixed doubles champion from the 2024 Paris Olympics, made a flying start against world No 154 Draxl, surging into a 4-0 lead in ‌the first set. But what had looked like an easy win for the Czech turned into a real battle as Draxl fought back to force a decider. Machac regained control by breaking ‌for a 4-2 lead ​in the third before sealing ‌victory in an hour and 55 minutes.

item.title: NFL Thanksgiving week games: Ranking the 5 weekday games by what's on the line
item.description: The NFL went out of its way to schedule five compelling matchups for Thanksgiving Eve, Thanksgiving and Black Friday. The schedule comes out in May, and things can change dramatically over six months. Yet four of the five matchups have held up very well. That's not a bad percentage, even if the Eagles and Cowboys have let us down. Everyone will watch those two marquee franchises anyway. There's a lot on the line in terms of the playoff race during this week. We rank the most important games, in terms of what's at stake. 1. Chiefs at Bills We could look back on this game as the one that determined where the AFC championship game is played. The Bills lead the conference at 9-1, but the 8-2 Chiefs can pull even with a win and also clinch the head-to-head tiebreaker. The 8-2 Broncos also will have a big say in the race for the No. 1 seed, as could the Jaguars and Bengals who are each 7-3. But a big part of the playoff picture will be revealed in the primetime Thanksgiving game. The Bills are trying to win their first Super Bowl, and a No. 1 seed would help that quest. The Bills are 0-4 in the playoffs against the Chiefs in the Josh Allen/Patrick Mahomes era but three of those games came in Kansas City. A win Thursday night would probably ensure the Bills don't have to play at Arrowhead Stadium in January. Josh Allen has consistently felt the pain from the Chiefs in big games. (AP Photo/ Jeffrey T. Barnes) ASSOCIATED PRESS 2. Bears at Lions The game will go a long way in determining the NFC North race. The Bears and Lions are tied for first place at 8-2, and the winner Thursday will have a one-game lead and an edge in the tiebreaker. They meet again in Week 17, but Thursday will shape the race over December. The Vikings aren't out of the race either at 7-3, and the Packers are still lingering at 6-4. The NFC North is really good, and whoever wins it will have earned it. The Lions keep overcoming injuries and have won six in a row. The Bears are on a roll too; they haven't trailed during a five-game winning streak. There was a long stretch in which the Lions' traditional Thanksgiving game didn't matter much because they weren't very good. Detroit has gotten a lot better and this game is one of the most important of the season in terms of division races. 3. Packers at Rams The NFL practically invented a Thanksgiving Eve holiday as an excuse to put a game on Wednesday. At least it made it a good matchup. This game is huge in a competitive NFC wild-card race. The Rams' chances of going to the playoffs would rise from 34% to 47% with a win, according to The Athletic, while the Packers' playoff odds would fall from 40% to 25%. If the Packers win they'll have a 61% chance of making it while the Rams' odds would fall all the way to 16%. It's stunning to think that with a loss, the overwhelming preseason Super Bowl favorite would have worse than a one-in-five shot of even making the postseason field. item.title: Guirassy makes bold claim about his place among world's best strikers
item.description: Guirassy makes bold claim about his place among world's best strikers Borussia Dortmund striker Serhou Guirassy believes he belongs among the world's top five forwards and has not ruled out winning the Ballon d'Or . In an interview with “ Bild” , the 30-year-old also opened up about his relationship with Fábio Silva and his future at the Bundesliga club. Asked whether he receives enough recognition, Guirassy made a confident assessment of his position in world football. "If you look at the last three or four years, there are strikers like Kane and Mbappé – and I would say that I might be fourth or fifth ," he explained. The Dortmund forward also believes the Ballon d'Or is within reach, despite finishing 21st in the 2025 voting. "Anything is possible for anyone – including me. For me, football is always about the moment," Guirassy said. "If you have a great season with your team, anything can happen." One of the keys to Dortmund's success could be the partnership between Guirassy and Fábio Silva. The Guinea international insists there is no rivalry between the two forwards. "He is like my little brother. I don't see Fábio as competition. My competition is myself. I want to be better every day than I was the day before," he said. Guirassy also praised Silva's versatility, adding that the pair have shown they can play together and support each other. Finally, the 30-year-old addressed speculation about his long-term future. His current contract runs until 2028, but an extension is certainly something he could imagine. "There was a period when I wasn't happy. Today, I am very happy. And fundamentally, I can imagine it " , Guirassy revealed. "Dortmund are a top club. I want to win something here and I feel comfortable."

item.title: Jets Win Proves Geno Smith Deserves A Return Contract
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images The New York Jets beat the Los Angeles Chargers 27-24 on Sunday night at SoFi Stadium. This win ended a five-game losing streak and gave the team its third victory of the season. While the 3-8 record looks bad on paper, the performance showed real signs of life. The offense moved the ball with a balance the team has not seen in years. This game proves the Jets can win even when the defense struggles. The Quarterback Is Playing Well Geno Smith delivered a perfect game for the Jets. He threw three touchdowns and gained 176 yards on 17 of 21 completions. ESPN’s Rich Cimini noted that this was Smith’s fourth game with three touchdown passes and an 80 percent completion rate. No other Jets quarterback has reached that mark more than three times in franchise history. Smith has 15 touchdowns against just three interceptions this year. He is the reason this offense works. The team should not look to replace him in 2027. Aaron Glenn Sees Real Progress Head coach Aaron Glenn praised the offensive unit after the game. He told reporters, “We did a really good job of being balanced, scoring in the red zone.” Glenn also highlighted how well the team used its playmakers. He said, “Getting pressure players the ball so those guys can make plays. I thought we orchestrated the drives the way we wanted. That was good to see.” The defense still has major issues, but the offense is finally clicking. Shepard And Bailey Shine Sterling Shepard stepped up in a big way with two touchdown catches. Glenn called him “The Energizer bunny. That’s who he is.” The coach added, “He has so much juice, and he loves playing the game. He really does. I’m glad we have him.” Rookie David Bailey also made his mark with two more sacks, bringing his season total to 9.5. He is on pace to break a rookie sack record set nearly 30 years ago. The Jets have talent, but they must fix their clock management to win more games. The next matchup is Sunday, Nov. 29, at Hard Rock Stadium against the Miami Dolphins.

item.title: ESPN analyst makes bold projection about Puka Nacua's future with the Rams
item.description: ESPN analyst makes bold projection about Puka Nacua's future with the Rams originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams are coming up on a high-profile game against the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve, and the excitement is building. However, looking past this one game, there's an elephant in the room that the team will need to address. One of the biggest talking points right now for the Rams is if they're going to extend star wide receiver Puka Nacua. It's a sticky situation, because Nacua has two major issues right now. He has a knee injury that needs surgery and also landed a three-game NFL suspension. But despite these things, ESPN thinks he's worth extending. ESPN believes the Los Angeles Rams should extend Puka Nacua despite his issues In a feature released on Tuesday going into detail about all of the NFL teams heading into Week 12 , ESPN's Sarah Barshop says the team should extend Nacua. "The Rams have a long list of potential free agents, including Nacua, defensive tackle Kobie Turner, edge rusher Byron Young, wide receiver Davante Adams and guard Kevin Dotson," she notes. "But Nacua has been a difference-maker to this Rams offense since his historic rookie season." She adds that before his season-ending knee injury, Nacua's 70 receptions were the "most through a player's first seven games of a season in NFL history, per ESPN Research." "As the Rams make a decision, they will have to weigh Nacua's injury history and off-field incidents," she adds. "But it would be a surprise to see him leave in free agency, whether that takes a franchise tag or an extension." It's true that Nacua has a really messy situation. Some players aren't worth the drama. But Nacua is probably worth it. item.title: Florian Wirtz reveals how Jurgen Klopp has helped his Liverpool performances
item.description: Florian Wirtz reveals how Jurgen Klopp has helped his Liverpool performances Florian Wirtz finding rhythm at Liverpool through fitness, adaptation and quiet guidance Florian Wirtz has started to look like the player Liverpool thought they were buying for £116 million. The numbers say it clearly, the performances back it up, and the context matters too. In the 4-0 win over Manchester United, Wirtz scored once and created another. He met Rio Ngumoha’s cross with a volley in the 13th minute and later set up Victor Munoz for the fourth. That took him to two goals and four assists in 11 Premier League appearances this season, all of them starts. He has also created 33 chances, more than any other player in the division. That is a marked step up from his first league campaign at Anfield, when he managed five goals and three assists in 33 appearances after arriving from Bayer Leverkusen in a deal that made him the most expensive player in British football at the time. Physical gains driving Wirtz form Players adapt at different speeds. For Wirtz, the adjustment appears to have been physical as much as technical. English football asks different questions. The tempo is harsher, the duels are constant, and creative players get far less time to organise themselves. Right now, Wirtz looks more capable of dealing with all of it. That matters because his talent was never the issue. The issue was whether he could impose it often enough. This season, he is doing exactly that. He is seeing more of the ball in dangerous areas, affecting games earlier and producing decisive moments instead of neat touches that go nowhere. Photo: IMAGO Klopp advice helping Liverpool adaptation Wirtz has also opened up on the role Jürgen Klopp has played in helping him settle, even after Klopp’s Liverpool reign ended in 2024. Now working with Germany, Klopp has remained a useful sounding board. “Of course we are speaking always about Liverpool,” Wirtz said. “When we have the time to speak about things like that. He had a great time here and he’s a coach who stayed here the most in his career.” Wirtz made it clear that the advice is not about systems or shape. It is more human than that, and probably more useful for a player trying to establish himself in a new country and at a demanding club. “He tells me all the time that he loved his time here, the people love him here and tries to give me some advice to get successful over here as he has shown how it is done.” He added, “It’s always small things. More private things. But he is speaking good about the club, the region here, the people, and that helps to hear someone who has experienced it for a long time. “It’s really good that he knows a lot about this club. item.description: Newcastle United keen on move for 20-year-old defender Newcastle Transfer News: Dies Janse on Ajax Shortlist as Defensive Planning Continues Newcastle United are tracking Ajax defender Dies Janse as part of their wider recruitment drive for emerging defensive talent, according to TeamTalk . The 20-year-old has been identified as a player with clear upside, and the interest appears to sit within a longer-term strategy rather than any immediate push to complete a deal. The report states that Newcastle “have begun tracking Ajax centre-back Dies Janse” and that they are “one of four Premier League sides keen on the defender”. That points to a competitive situation developing around a player who is increasingly gaining attention across Europe. Janse’s profile is easy to understand. He is described as a defender whose “versatility is a major asset”, with the Dutchman able to operate as both a left-sided centre-back and at left-back. For clubs building squads with flexibility in mind, that sort of adaptability carries obvious value, particularly in a market where specialist left-footed defenders are often difficult to secure. Dies Janse fits Newcastle recruitment model Newcastle’s interest also aligns with the club’s growing focus on young players who can develop into first-team options. TeamTalk reports that the aim is to strengthen their “pipeline of young defensive talent”, which speaks to succession planning as much as immediate squad depth. Janse spent the 2025/26 season on loan at FC Groningen, where he “established himself as a regular starter”, making 31 league appearances and scoring twice. Since returning to Ajax, he has made 15 senior appearances and is now pushing for a more prominent role. Those numbers matter, because they show a player already tested in senior football while still early in his development. Ajax have already moved to protect their position. The Dutch club extended his contract until June 2030 last September, after what the report describes as “growing interest from across Europe’s top leagues”. Club Brugge were also said to be strongly linked earlier in the year, underlining that Newcastle are far from alone in their admiration. Sporting director Jordi Cruijff has acknowledged the attention around Janse, while the report adds that Ajax view the situation through the lens of previous defensive exits. They are “determined not to lose another highly rated centre-back too easily”, with parallels drawn to Sven Botman’s departure before his eventual move to Newcastle. For now, this looks like monitoring rather than active negotiations. item.title: Swayman’s Slump Can’t Continue If Bruins Want To Win
item.description: Bob DeChiara-Imagn Images The Boston Bruins cannot afford to ignore the dip in form from their starting goaltender. In three of his last four matches, Jeremy Swayman allowed four or more goals, leaving the team in a perilous spot. Although he appeared solid after stopping 22 shots for one goal versus the Detroit Red Wings, that performance was an outlier. On Saturday night versus the Washington Capitals, he reverted to the shaky form seen during the Montreal and Minnesota games. The team has won four of his six starts in November, but that path relies too much on luck and an offense that is just starting to find its rhythm. The Numbers Are Getting Ugly Statistical reality is catching up to the Bruins’ starter. For the month of November, Swayman now holds a 3.25 goals-against average alongside an .890 save percentage. Those numbers are not good enough for a team that wants to sit at the top of the Atlantic Division. While some might argue the Bruins have a better offense than people think, the team has shown enough stagnant nights from its best players to know they are one slump away from ugly losses. When Swayman performs at his peak, those poor nights become irrelevant. When he is not, hope begins to fade among the fanbase. Bad Months Happen But Confidence Is Key A bad month is not an anomaly for Swayman, but the way he is letting in goals recently shows a lack of confidence. He experienced many rough months before holding out until training camp, and even his massive bounce-back season included a December where his save percentage fell below .900. The real value of this goalie does not show up in counting stats because he gets plastered with shots every night due to defensive lapses. The low save percentage is bad, but the style of goals allowed is what makes him look like a goalie with hurt confidence. The Bench Is Right There Bruins fans have good news because Michael DiPietro sits right behind him in the rankings. Despite placing near the league peak in goals saved above expected during the prior two seasons, Swayman has since dropped to 11th after a few poor performances. DiPietro sits in 12th place, which is close enough to cause worry if the starter does not turn it around. Although some might argue it is time to grant the rookie goaltender more opportunities, the sparse schedule usually favors the starter to maintain rhythm. The Bruins need their No. 1 to fix this now.

item.title: Gasperini speaks ahead of PSG-Roma: “Tomorrow we must show our personality.”
item.description: Gasperini speaks ahead of PSG-Roma: “Tomorrow we must show our personality.” After finishing their training at Trigoria, Roma arrived in Paris on the eve of the highly anticipated match against Luis Enrique’s PSG. Gian Piero Gasperini presented the match at a press conference, addressing issues related to his possible options and more. The Giallorossi coach commented on the matchup against a giant of modern football: “It’s the first time we’ve faced PSG. We’ll have to understand their parameters, hopefully reducing their effectiveness.” Regarding the early comebacks in the competition, the coach said: “The Champions League is the most important competition in the world. You can put in great performances, but there are also incidents, and the best players around.” Gasp recalled the match against Atalanta: “The match against Atalanta was tough. We were down to 10 men, but this is a different game. Roma is approaching this competition after years, and for us it’s a measure of what we’re doing.” Then the general from Grugliasco discussed the solutions he will adopt to limit his opponents: “Clearly, in these types of matches, more solutions are needed; we don’t have any previous parameters. Beyond tactics, personality will be important, as will the ability to counter their play.” The Parisians will have several injuries, but that won’t be a problem for them: “There’s no scientific answer to injuries. There’s been a great improvement in diagnoses, and PSG still has a squad that allows them to make up for absences. As I said before, PSG is a team that knows how to compensate for the absences of very strong players with organization and with substitutes, who are absolutely valuable.” The matches against Real Madrid and Manchester United can teach us something. “This is the Champions League, a competition of incidents. You have to be excellent in every situation, there are some great players and sometimes it’s not even enough to put in strong performances, even though I think that’s the best way to get results. You have to be careful about mistakes because they often pay the price.”

item.title: McLaren Boss Sanna Hints At Major Grasser Racing Move For 2027
item.description: McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown's office is seen Tuesday, Feb. 3, 2026, during a tour of the new McLaren Racing Center in Indianapolis. McLaren is evaluating new drivers and seeking additional partners to expand globally. Giorgio Sanna, the head of motorsport at McLaren, did not deny reports that the Grasser Racing Team and driver Mirko Bortolotti could jump ship for the 2027 season. Sanna spoke to Motorsport.com on Tuesday about the rumors swirling around the Austrian outfit. “Now it’s too early to talk about it, but for sure there are a few top teams that are looking with interest on McLaren Motorsport for the future,” Sanna said. The Italian executive knows Grasser well, having won many races with them during their time at Lamborghini. The Vision Comes First Respect for the past does not mean the team will ignore its future goals. Sanna made it clear that history with Grasser is nice, but the long-term plan for McLaren matters more. “Of course, I have a lot of estimation on Grasser Racing Team (sic). We won a lot together, but we have to take in consideration the targets and the plan and the vision of McLaren,” he says. The team needs to fill a gap in Asia, a market they currently lack a presence in. The strategy involves bringing in international teams from Europe, the Americas, and Asia to build a truly global force. Sanna noted that the brand is growing properly and needs the right partners to match that momentum. “Let’s see if there will be a chance,” he added, leaving the door open for a formal agreement soon. The focus remains on expanding the program and becoming a global player, as Sanna confirmed to reporters. More Than One Team Interested Grasser is not the only outfit circling the McLaren garage. Sanna admitted that the interest extends beyond a single team, suggesting a broader push for new alliances. The boss believes the current success of the cars and the team culture is driving this demand from other racing groups. From 2028, McLaren plans to sell its new GT3 car to as many teams as possible, turning the brand into a major supplier. Sanna stated that he has “a lot of conversations with many teams” and expects news on new partners quite soon. The move could reshape the grid if the right deal is struck before the season starts.

item.title: Orioles Spend Franchise-Record $125 Million in Deal for Pitcher
item.description: Oct 26, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta (51) looks on from the dugout after a pitching change against the Milwaukee Brewers during the fifth inning in game three of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Less than a day after watching left-hander Trevor Rogers depart for the Chicago Cubs on a five-year, $120 million contract, the Baltimore Orioles moved quickly to replace him. On Tuesday, the club agreed to terms with free-agent right-hander Freddy Peralta on a five-year, $125 million deal, according to multiple reports. The contract contains no opt-outs and no deferred money and remains pending a physical. The $25 million average annual value is the largest commitment the Orioles have ever made to a pitcher. Peralta, who turns 31 next June, becomes the clear front-of-the-rotation arm for a staff that already features Kyle Bradish and Shane Baz. Peralta’s path to Baltimore was circuitous. The Brewers traded him to the Mets last January with one year remaining on his contract. After posting a 4.99 ERA in 22 starts with New York, he was dealt to the Rays at the 2026 trade deadline. In Tampa Bay, he stabilized, going 5-2 with a 3.25 ERA across 10 starts and 55⅓ innings. He then elevated his profile in October, winning ALCS MVP honors after helping the Rays reach the World Series. In the postseason, he logged a 2.95 ERA over 21⅓ innings. For the full season, Peralta finished 10-11 with a 4.42 ERA in 169 innings. Career-wise, he is 80-53 with a 3.71 ERA and more than 1,300 strikeouts across parts of nine seasons, with two All-Star appearances on his résumé. Because he was traded midseason, he was ineligible for a qualifying offer and costs Baltimore no draft compensation. Outside the Peralta agreement, the Orioles’ free-agent activity this winter has been modest. They avoided arbitration with closer Félix Bautista on a one-year, $2.35 million deal and have signed several minor-league free agents (including infielder José Barrero and others). They also added multiple players to the 40-man roster ahead of the potential Rule 5 draft and claimed right-hander Braden Nett off waivers. The major-league rotation and lineup, however, had not received a significant free-agent infusion until Peralta’s deal. With the collective bargaining agreement set to expire on December 1 and a lockout widely expected, the window for further big-ticket moves is short. Baltimore still appears to be looking for additional pitching depth —particularly a left-hander—and could explore further roster upgrades before any work stoppage.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
